text: MOUNT BLOCKER FOUND, and it is an external dependency not an engineering gap. The assisted-order service refuses every submission unless deps.legal supplies the required agreement set: service.ts requireAgreements throws legal_requirements_unavailable when the port is absent, and matching is EXACT so a version alias like 'current' can never satisfy a requirement. createAssistedOrderProductionComposition in production.ts does not accept or pass a legal port at all (zero occurrences of 'legal' in that file), so the production composition as written can never accept a submission. That fail-closed behaviour is correct and must not be weakened. The client names three agreement kinds: assisted_order_accuracy, assisted_order_contact_consent, assisted_order_request_notice. Each needs an APPROVED VERSION STRING from counsel, and versions cannot be invented: the whole point of the exact-match design is that the submission records the precise (kind, version) pairs the customer saw. A canonical legal registry already exists in this repo and is the right source to adapt (server/research/early-access/legal/package-completion.ts, membership-activation/signatures.ts, commerce/production-deps.ts all consume requiredAgreements), so the wiring is small once the versions exist. SECOND GAP, engineering only: the wall admits /early-access/assisted-orders/config and client api.ts loadAssistedOrderConfig calls it, but createAssistedOrderRouteTable in http.ts publishes NO /config descriptor. Mounting without adding one means that call falls through to the SPA catch-all and returns 200 HTML, which the client would fail to parse. The config route is where enabled:false belongs while the legal set is unavailable, so the wizard tells the customer up front instead of after they fill the form. RECOMMENDED MOUNT ORDER: add the config descriptor returning enabled:false until legal is wired, mount everything else, and keep the submit door refusing. That ships a truthful surface without fabricating legal acceptance.
